title_en: Character Riddles (7/20): A Very Young Character
note_en: Spoken Chinese has a single word tā for "he," "she," and "it"; only writing tells them apart: 他 (he), 她 (she), 它 (it). As the teacher says, “他”“她”“它”在口语里发音完全一样 "they sound exactly the same in speech." So when listening, English speakers have to work out from context who tā is, something English settles with separate words.
